database.title: Temporal
database.blurb: The persistence schema of the Temporal server for PostgreSQL 12 and later, plus the standard visibility store. There are no foreign keys: every table carries shard_id and namespace_id (or a queue type) and the server keeps rows consistent itself, which is deliberate for a sharded, high-write store.

domains.title: Namespaces
domains.blurb: Registered namespaces and the metadata row that versions them.

domains.title: Shards and executions
domains.blurb: Shard ownership, the mutable state of every workflow execution, the current run per workflow id, buffered events, and the CHASM node tree.

domains.title: Mutable state maps
domains.blurb: Per-execution maps keyed by shard, namespace, workflow and run: activities, timers, child workflows, cancel and signal requests.

domains.title: Event history
domains.blurb: The append-only history nodes and the branch tree that lets runs share prefixes.

domains.title: Task queues (matching)
domains.blurb: Workflow and activity tasks waiting for a worker, the queues that hold them, per-queue user data and build-id routing. The v2 tables are the fairness-aware successors.

domains.title: History service task queues
domains.blurb: The internal queues the history service works through: immediate and scheduled tasks, transfer, timer, replication (with its dead-letter queue) and visibility tasks.

domains.title: Queues and cluster
domains.blurb: Generic persistence queues and their metadata, the newer queue tables, cluster metadata and membership.

domains.title: Nexus
domains.blurb: Nexus endpoints and the partition status row that versions them.

domains.title: Visibility
domains.blurb: The standard visibility store: one denormalised row per execution for listing and search.

conventions: Tables are keyed by shard_id and namespace_id; there are no foreign keys, and the server enforces consistency.
Binary protobuf payloads live in data / data_encoding column pairs.
